name: search_question_library
description: Search the published question library. Returns question definitions only - never response data.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the question slug and id.

name: list_questions
description: List the question library with each question's latest version and its status, draft and deprecated versions included. Definitions only, never response data.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the question slug and id.

name: read_question
description: Read one question: its versions with their statuses, and the complete definition of the version you name (label, help, type, required, constraints, messages and options). Authoring content only.

questionId.description: The question to read. Defaults to the question the current screen is about.

version.description: Which version's definition to return. The newest version when absent.

name: diff_question_versions
description: Compare two versions of a question and report which members of the definition differ, by name. The names only, never their content. A version that does not exist is MISSING, not identical and not unchanged: `outcome` is then `unavailable`, `fromFound` or `toFound` says which side is absent, and `identical` and `changedFields` are null. An empty `changedFields` means the two versions were compared and nothing differs, which only ever happens when both sides exist.

questionId.description: The question to read. Defaults to the question the current screen is about.

name: question_recipes
description: Look up this installation's own recipe for one or more common question types: the settings to apply, what the product cannot express, and what to tell the person about it. Name only types the list holds. Reads nothing a user authored and changes nothing.

types.description: The question types to look up, from this list.

name: propose_questions
description: Stage new question definitions for the apply-draft card, and nothing else. It creates nothing: the definitions are kept only by an apply-draft card proposed in the same turn, and are discarded otherwise. To create a question the user keeps, propose a question.create step instead.

questions.description: New question definitions to add to the library. Not published by this call.

name: propose_draft
description: Propose the complete draft FormDefinition for the form this builder screen is about. Returns the advisory validation issues that would block a publish, and the warnings that would not. It saves nothing: follow it with the apply-draft action, which is the only thing that keeps it. It exists on the form builder alone; elsewhere, save a draft with a form.saveDraft step instead.

definition.description: The complete proposed draft FormDefinition, replacing the current draft wholesale.

name: validate_draft
description: Run the publish validation over the draft you have proposed this turn, or over the form's saved draft when you have proposed none, and return its blocking issues and its non-blocking warnings.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: project_draft
description: Project a form's draft for hypothetical answers and return which steps and questions a respondent would see. Reads no submitted answer. A draft with blocking issues cannot be projected: the result says so and names them.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

answers.description: Hypothetical answers to project the draft against, keyed by question id. These are the model's own hypotheses; no submitted answer is ever read.

name: test_rule
description: Evaluate one of a form's rules against hypothetical answers and report whether its condition matched. Reads no submitted answer and changes nothing.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

ruleId.description: The rule to evaluate, by its ruleId.

answers.description: Hypothetical answers to evaluate the rule against, keyed by answer key. These are the model's own hypotheses; no submitted answer is ever read.

instances.description: Hypothetical repeating-group instance ids, keyed by group id.

name: read_form
description: Read one form: its slug and title, whether it has a draft, its latest published version, which version is live in the current environment, its steps with their question counts, its rule ids, the question versions its draft pins unpublished, and the COMPLETE working draft under `definition`. Start any form.saveDraft from that definition: a draft save replaces the draft wholesale, so anything you leave out is dropped.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: search_forms
description: Search the forms this caller may read, by slug or id, and report each one's latest version and the one live in the current environment.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the form slug and id.

name: list_form_versions
description: List one form's published versions, each with when it was published, which environments it is live in, and its step and question counts.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: diff_form_versions
description: Compare two published versions of a form, or one of them against its working draft (null), and report which steps, pinned questions and rules differ. A side that does not exist is MISSING, not empty: `outcome` is then `unavailable`, `fromFound` or `toFound` says which side is absent, and every comparison field is null. A form with no working draft comes back that way, so never read it as a draft that has been emptied. Structure only: no authored text and no response data.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: list_releases
description: Report this deployment's environments, which version of one form stands in each and whether it is closed, plus that form's publish history with who put each version live and who approved.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: count_links
description: Count a form's secure links by state in the current environment. No link URL or token exists to return.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: list_links
description: List a form's secure links in the current environment with each one's state, whether it is single-use and when it expires. No link URL or token exists to return.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: list_responses
description: List a form's responses under the response list's own four filters, metadata only: session id, times, version, access mode and flag state. Never an answer value.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound on the start time.

to.description: Exclusive upper bound on the start time.

name: count_responses
description: Count a form's responses under the response list's own four filters. Never an answer value.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound on the start time.

to.description: Exclusive upper bound on the start time.

name: delivery_status
description: Report a form's webhook endpoints and the state of their recent deliveries: counts by state and the attempt bound that was scanned. Never a payload, a consumer response body or an error string.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

webhookId.description: One of this form's endpoints, or every endpoint when absent.

name: list_webhooks
description: List a form's webhook endpoints in the current environment and their recent deliveries with each one's state, attempts and last HTTP status. Never a payload, a consumer response body or an error string.

formId.description: The form to read. Defaults to the form the current screen is about.

name: count_dead_letters
description: Count the dead-letter queue, by form, within the bound it scanned. Never a payload.

name: list_erasures
description: List the erasure log for the current environment: which session was erased, from which form and version, when and why. The log holds no answers.

name: list_workspaces
description: List the workspaces this caller administers, with whether each is the shared library and whether it has Second approval on for a publish to prod.

name: read_workspace
description: Read one workspace's members with their roles, and its access groups with the role, environments and forms each group grants.

workspaceId.description: The workspace to read. Defaults to the workspace the current screen is about.

name: propose_plan
description: Propose an ordered plan of actions for the user to review and confirm once. A single action is a plan of one step. It runs nothing: the user sees a card with every step and every argument in full and confirms it on the screen's own control. An argument may reference an earlier step's result as { fromStep, field }, at most one such reference per step. The plan stops at the first failure. Returns whether the proposal was accepted, or the reason it was refused. The sentence you write immediately before this call is quoted on the card as its reason and stays there after the card has run, so make it say WHY the plan does what it does. Name neither the card nor its state anywhere in it, at its start no less than at its end, and say nothing about what their Confirm will do: "The plan is on a card for you to confirm.", "The card is up.", "waiting for your Confirm" and "Nothing changes until you confirm it." all say what the card already says, and each one is wrong the moment they confirm it. Give a plan of more than one step a title as well: what it leaves behind, in the person's own words, which the card uses as its heading.

anyOf.description: The slug the form is addressed by. The form id is derived from it once and never changes, so a mistyped slug is permanent.
The locale the first draft is authored in, such as en or en-AU.
The workspace the form belongs to. Omitted where the installation has one, and required where it has more.

Create a form and its empty first draft in a workspace this user may create in. The id is made from the slug and never changes. The form's title is authored in the builder afterwards; creating it changes nothing a respondent can reach.

Apply the draft you proposed with propose_draft to this form's working draft, for the user to review as a diff and confirm. Call propose_draft first. It publishes nothing and puts nothing live: the draft is stored as a draft and marked agent-assisted.
The form whose draft this replaces. Name an earlier step's result where that step creates the form.
The complete draft: defaultLocale, title, steps and rules. Leave formId out of it; the step's own formId argument is the form, and the server fills it in.

Save a complete draft to a form, through the same save path every edit in the builder takes. It publishes nothing and puts nothing live: the draft is stored as a draft and marked agent-assisted. This is how a form goes from blank to a reviewable draft, after form.create and any question.create steps of the same plan.
The one environment the newly frozen version goes live in.

Publish the form's working draft to one environment: freeze it as the next version and make that version live there, in one act. Needs Edit forms and Publish forms for that environment. Where a non-prod environment exists a draft is never published straight to prod. The workflow and second approval apply exactly as they do on the screen.

Publish an existing version to one environment, including an earlier one (rollback). Nothing is frozen. Prod accepts only a version already live in a non-prod environment, where one exists. The workflow revision, the destination's current state and second approval are all rechecked at confirmation, so a stale review is refused and writes nothing, exactly as on the screen.
Whether a respondent must pass the challenge before submitting.
The minimum time on the form, or null to use the deployment's own floor.
Change the form's abuse-control settings. It affects sessions started from now on and leaves every session already under way untouched.
Close the form to new sessions in the current environment. Every session already under way keeps its pinned version and finishes normally.
Reopen the form to new sessions in the current environment.
How many links to mint.
When the links stop working, as a full UTC instant such as 2026-12-31T23:59:59.000Z.
Whether each link is consumed by the first respondent.

Create one-time or reusable respondent links for a form, in the environment the person's screen is set to. You do not choose that environment and cannot name another one. A link reaches the form only where that form is already live, so read the form first and say which environment the links are for before they confirm. expiresAt must be an instant still to come: one already past is refused when they confirm. Where they want to see what a lapsed link does, propose one a few minutes ahead and say in your reply when it lapses, rather than asking them how long it should last. The card shows that instant in their own zone rather than as you wrote it. The URLs are shown to the user once and are never returned to you.
Revoke one respondent link in the current environment.
Why the data is being erased. It is recorded on the tombstone.
Erase one respondent's answers and submission, recording a tombstone. It cannot be undone, and the user retypes the session id on the card before it can run.
Let one flagged response's withheld submission event through, so its consumers receive it.
The file format the download produces.
One row per answer, or one row per submission. CSV only.
The version whose shape the export follows. Required for a wide CSV.
The first day of the range, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The last day of the range, as YYYY-MM-DD.
Open the export dialog with these filters. The user presses Export and the file downloads in their browser; no part of it is returned to you.
The endpoint's full URL, with its query string if it has one.
Whether deliveries start at once.
Configure a new delivery endpoint for this form in the current environment. Its signing secret is shown to the user once and is never returned to you.
Replace an endpoint's signing secret. Deliveries signed with the old one stop verifying, and the new secret is shown to the user once.
The endpoint's full URL, with its query string if it has one.
Point an endpoint at another URL. The card names the endpoint and shows the new target in full, query string included.
Put a deactivated endpoint back in service in the current environment.
Stop delivering to an endpoint. The row and its delivery history stay, and a delivery already in flight keeps its own retry state.
Reset one dead-lettered delivery to due-now, so the worker attempts it again. It reads no part of the payload.
The group's name, unique within the workspace. It is a label, not a rule.
Every role each holder of this group is granted.
The environments the group applies in. There is no value meaning all of them. Empty only where every role in the group is forms.viewer or forms.editor, which apply in every environment.
Create an access group in a workspace. The group grants nobody anything until somebody holds it, so creating one changes no access by itself.
Remove an access group and every grant it carried. Each holder loses that access at once, and one revoke row is written for each.
The address of the person the group is granted to.
Grant an access group to one person, by address. A self-grant of a response role is held for another administrator to approve while the workspace has second approval on.
Revoke one person from an access group. Everybody else in it keeps theirs.
The member row's new role.
Make a member an owner of the workspace, or take ownership away. Removing the last owner is refused.
Whether a publish to prod and a response self-grant need a second account.
Change the workspace's Second approval switch: whether a publish to prod and a response self-grant need a second account.
The slug the question is addressed by, unique in the library.

The question definition, as the kernel takes it: `questionId`, `type`, `label` and whatever that type requires. The API refuses one that is not valid, and the card shows every field of it before anybody confirms.
The workspace the question belongs to. Omitted where the installation has one, and required where it has more.

Create a question and its first draft version in the library. The id is made once and never changes. Nothing pins the question until a form's draft does, and nothing serves it until the version is published.
The version this act names. A draft for a save, a published one to deprecate.

The question definition, as the kernel takes it: `questionId`, `type`, `label` and whatever that type requires. The API refuses one that is not valid, and the card shows every field of it before anybody confirms.
Replace a draft version's definition. A published or deprecated version is refused: published content is immutable, so changing one means opening a new version.
The version this act names. A draft for a save, a published one to deprecate.
Freeze a draft version and make it pinnable. Its content can never change again, and a form's draft that pins it stops reporting an unpublished pin.
The version this act names. A draft for a save, a published one to deprecate.
Block new pins on a published version. Every form already pinned to it is untouched and keeps serving it.
Open a new draft version, seeded from the latest one. Nothing published changes, and no form moves to it until a draft pins the new version.

steps.description: The steps in the order they run. A single action is a plan of one step. One plan, one Confirm.

thenAnother.description: True only where a second card has to follow this one, which is the case you say one sentence about before this one goes up. The screen gives you a turn as soon as every step here has run, so you put that next card up yourself and the person does not have to ask again. Leave it out otherwise: a card they did not ask for is never promised and never put up.

title.description: What this plan leaves behind, in a few plain words, which the card uses as its heading: "Ask about allergies, then publish to test". Name the outcome rather than the last step. No id and none of the words you may never write to the person, or the plan is refused. Leave it out and the card titles itself.

fromStep.description: The zero-based index of an earlier step.

field.description: A result field that step returns.

StepReference_d3.description: A reference to an earlier step's result, resolved when the plan runs.

name: edit_question
description: Place, move or remove one library question on the open draft of the form this builder is about. pin adds a published library question to a step; repin changes the version a question is pinned at; move puts a question on another step or at another position; unpin takes it off the form. It applies to the draft as this turn's earlier edits left it and returns what would still stop a publish. Nothing is saved until the turn ends, when the person's browser saves each edit with an Undo. It never creates or changes a library question: that is a propose_plan card.

action.description: pin adds a published library question to a step; repin changes the version it pins; move puts it on another step or position; unpin removes it from the form.

version.description: The library version to pin. Required by pin and repin.

stepId.description: The step to place it on. Required by pin and move.

position.description: Zero-based index to place it at. The end when absent.

name: edit_step
description: Add, replace, move or remove one step of the open draft of the form this builder is about. replace carries the whole step, its title and items, repeating groups included. It applies to the draft as this turn's earlier edits left it and returns what would still stop a publish. Nothing is saved until the turn ends, when the person's browser saves each edit with an Undo.

action.description: add inserts a new step; replace swaps one step for the step given, title and items included; move changes its position; remove deletes it.

step.description: The whole step, whose stepId must equal stepId. Required by add and replace.

position.description: Zero-based index to place it at. The end when absent.

name: edit_rule
description: Add or replace one visibility rule of the open draft by its ruleId, or remove one. It applies to the draft as this turn's earlier edits left it and returns what would still stop a publish. Nothing is saved until the turn ends, when the person's browser saves each edit with an Undo.

action.description: set adds the rule or replaces the one with this ruleId; remove deletes it.

rule.description: The whole rule, whose ruleId must equal ruleId. Required by set.

name: edit_copy
description: Change the wording of the open draft: the form's title, a step's title, or a repeating group's label or instance label. Wording only. It applies to the draft as this turn's earlier edits left it. Nothing is saved until the turn ends, when the person's browser saves each edit with an Undo.

stepId.description: The step whose title changes. Required by step-title.

groupId.description: The repeating group whose wording changes. Required by the two group targets.

name: open_publish_wizard
description: Open the publish screen for the form this builder is about, where the person reviews every change since the last publish and publishes it themselves. It publishes nothing, takes no arguments and is offered only to someone who may publish forms.
